TASK ID: vertex-cover-to-set-cover

USER REQUEST:
Write a polynomial-time reduction from Vertex Cover to Set Cover. problems.py defines both problems: SOURCE is Vertex Cover and TARGET is Set Cover. The SOURCE and TARGET class docstrings give the exact instance formats, yes-conditions and edge cases.

PROBLEM DEFINITIONS (the SOURCE and TARGET docstrings from problems.py, complete as given here):

SOURCE = VertexCover
Vertex Cover.

Instance: {"n": n, "edges": [[u, v], ...], "k": k}
  * Vertices are 0..n-1. Edges are undirected pairs [u, v] with u != v;
    [u, v] and [v, u] are the same edge and may not both appear.
  * k is any integer.

Yes iff the graph has a vertex cover of AT MOST k vertices: a set of
vertices that includes at least one endpoint of every edge.

Edge cases: k < 0 is always no. A graph with no edges is yes for every
k >= 0 (the empty set covers it). k >= n is yes, since all vertices cover
every edge.

TARGET = SetCover
Set Cover.

Instance: {"universe_size": u, "sets": [[element, ...], ...], "k": k}
  * The universe is the elements 0..u-1.
  * Each set lists distinct elements of the universe, in any order. A set
    may be empty, and the same set may appear more than once.
  * k is any integer.

Yes iff AT MOST k of the sets together contain every element of the
universe.

Edge cases: k < 0 is always no. u = 0 is yes for every k >= 0 (choosing
no sets covers the empty universe). If some element is in no set, the
answer is no.

INPUT FILES: ["problems.py"]
WORKING DIRECTORY: /tmp/reduction-rm055yfk
All input files are in this directory; run every command from it and write your files here. problems.py is long (about 500 lines): you do not need to read it to know the formats, which are given above. It provides SOURCE and TARGET with is_yes(instance), validate(instance) and random_instance(rng, scale); search it (e.g. with grep) only if you need something specific.

REQUIRED OUTPUT: create reduce.py in the workspace, defining
    reduce(instance) -> instance
It takes an instance of the source problem and returns an instance of the target problem, both in the formats documented in problems.py. The answer to the returned instance must be yes exactly when the answer to the input instance is yes, and reduce must run in polynomial time. Do not call the brute-force solvers inside reduce.

You may read files such as problems.py, but do not run, execute or test any code. Write reduce.py, then submit.

+"""Reduction from Vertex Cover to Set Cover.
+
+The source problem (VertexCover) instance format is:
+    {"n": n, "edges": [[u, v], ...], "k": k}
+where vertices are numbered 0..n-1 and edges are undirected pairs.
+
+The target problem (SetCover) instance format is:
+    {"universe_size": u, "sets": [[element, ...], ...], "k": k}
+where the universe consists of elements 0..u-1.
+
+Reduction construction:
+    * Each edge of the graph becomes a distinct element of the universe.
+    * For every vertex v we create a set containing exactly those edge‑indices
+      that are incident to v.
+    * The budget k is kept unchanged.
+
+Correctness sketch:
+    * Selecting a vertex cover of size ≤ k corresponds to selecting the same
+      vertices (i.e., their incident‑edge sets) which together contain every
+      edge element – a set cover of size ≤ k.
+    * Conversely, any set cover of size ≤ k must consist of sets that are the
+      incident‑edge sets of some vertices, and those vertices cover all edges.
+    * Edge cases (k < 0, empty edge list, k ≥ n) are preserved because the
+      construction mirrors the original instance semantics.
+
+The reduction runs in time linear in the size of the graph, which is
+polynomial.
+"""
+
+from typing import Dict, List, Any
+
+
+def reduce(instance: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
+    """Convert a Vertex Cover instance to an equivalent Set Cover instance.
+
+    Parameters
+    ----------
+    instance:
+        A dictionary with keys ``n`` (int), ``edges`` (list of [u, v]), and
+        ``k`` (int) following the VertexCover specification.
+
+    Returns
+    -------
+    dict
+        A SetCover instance dictionary with keys ``universe_size``, ``sets``
+        and ``k``.
+    """
+    n: int = instance["n"]
+    edges: List[List[int]] = instance.get("edges", [])
+    k: int = instance["k"]
+
+    # Map each edge to a unique element index.
+    # The universe size is the number of edges.
+    m = len(edges)
+    universe_size = m
+
+    # Prepare a list of sets for each vertex.
+    # Using list of lists to match the expected format (distinct elements).
+    vertex_sets: List[List[int]] = [[] for _ in range(n)]
+
+    for idx, (u, v) in enumerate(edges):
+        # Add this edge index to the incident vertex sets.
+        vertex_sets[u].append(idx)
+        vertex_sets[v].append(idx)
+
+    # The SetCover instance expects a list of sets (order does not matter).
+    # We include a set for every vertex, even if it is empty (which is allowed).
+    sets = vertex_sets
+
+    return {
+        "universe_size": universe_size,
+        "sets": sets,
+        "k": k,
+    }
+
*** End Patch
PATCH"}
